rows.evidence: Q1: Sections III-V and Table I - the authors implement their trajectory equations in MATLAB and report their own model runs (time and position vectors, irrigation error, water used per segment versus a modelled traditional volume).
rows.notes: The study is a pure simulation. The CWSI input image is taken from Bellvert et al. (2014) for a Pinot-noir vineyard; the UAV trajectories, irrigated volumes and the resulting post-irrigation CWSI are computed from the model under assumptions of constant nozzle flow, uniform rectangular spray and grid paths. No UAV flight, no field irrigation and no measurement of actual water use or crop stress were performed, and the authors explicitly state that experimental tests to back up these results should still be carried out. Per the rating rules a model run never checked against observations is not own evidence on the claimed effect, so Q2 is 'no'. What the study actually shows: a simulated total saving of 3.12 L (31.5% of the 9.88 L used) and per-segment savings of 7.5% to 122.9% (expressed relative to the volume used, not to the traditional volume) compared with a modelled uniform irrigation sized to the driest point; the authors also acknowledge irrigation error up to about 50% at some points and imperfect coverage at segment ends. Although the paper mentions assumptions and model shortcomings (Conclusion), these are not credited because Q2 is 'no'.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a conference paper presenting a MATLAB simulation of UAV irrigation trajectories derived from a CWSI image; there is no field or experimental validation of water savings.
